entries.question: Can Overcenter maintain a reproducible total ordering of production-code importance from quantitative facts?
entries.claim: A revision-bound callable graph plus explicit authority/recovery semantics can derive an inspectable production-code criticality vector and a calibrated total order without ranking tests or experiments themselves.
entries.contrast: Periodically repeat a human ranking exercise or rely on generic complexity/hotspot metrics alone.
environment: Git with full repository history for revision-bound blame/change exposure
success_criteria: Only production callables under src/ enter the ranked population.
Configured authority and recovery selectors resolve exactly once.
The static graph is informative and unresolved internal calls are reported.
At least 80% of the initial pairwise calibration judgments agree.
Every surprising rank decomposes into quantitative vector components and graph evidence.
entries.interpretation: Treat the ranking as a revision-bound experimental projection. The vector components are durable inputs; the weighting policy and callable-level unit boundary remain replaceable.
non_claims: Callable boundaries are the final semantic unit.
Static test reachability is equivalent to hostile-case evidence.
Exported-entrypoint reachability is equivalent to production telemetry.
The current weighting equation is uniquely correct.
